problem: Full-context transformer RL policies must store and attend over ever-growing KV caches for long-horizon tasks, which is costly, unstable to train, and extrapolates poorly beyond the training context; recurrent fixed-size memories propagate gradients poorly.
motivation: Embodied agents in long-horizon, memory-intensive tasks (e.g., repeatedly finding objects in one house) must retain task-relevant information while discarding irrelevant input. Language-model context-compression ideas (Autocompressors, RMT) have not been adapted to RL, where credit assignment over long horizons requires gradients through the memory.
key_idea: Interleave periodic learned summary tokens into the transformer input during RL training, accumulate them as the only memory of past segments, and backpropagate the RL loss through all summaries.
insight: Two design choices matter. Propagating gradients across all summary segments is essential: AC with truncated BPTT does much worse than AC over all segments. Accumulating summaries beats fixed recurrent memory (RMT lags Memo by about 5% SR, and RMT-128 is unstable). Further ablations: summary length is sensitive (32 best, 64 worst), segment-length randomization matters, and re-encoding summaries beats building the KV cache directly from the summary embeddings. Compressed memory also makes streaming inference robust.
method: Segmented summarization: split the input into segments of l_seg (256) and append l_sum (32) learnable summary embeddings at the end of each segment so the transformer emits summary tokens (about 8x compression).

Accumulated memory buffer: all previous summary tokens are kept and attended to, together with the current segment's observations; older raw observations are masked, so the summaries form an information bottleneck.
End-to-end RL training: gradients flow through all summaries via attention, integrated with on-policy RELIC (DD-PPO) and off-policy AMAGO.
Positional encoding: positions are assigned relative to the segment, and summaries are re-indexed, so the position range stays bounded.
Segment length randomization: segment lengths are sampled within ±20% of l_seg during training, acting as regularization and a curriculum.
KV cache refresh: summary vectors are recomputed together with the KV cache after each policy update to keep memory consistent with the current weights.

setting.backbone: Small 4-layer LLaMA-style causal transformer (hidden 256, 8 heads) trained from scratch with a frozen finetuned VC-1 ViT-B visual encoder
setting.model_size: small (4 layers, 256 hidden dim) transformer, plus a ViT-B encoder
setting.training_data: ExtObjNav: 11,100 self-generated object placements over 37 HSSD training scenes, trained with RL for 700M-1B env steps; Dark-Key-To-Door via off-policy AMAGO; no extra or web data
setting.observation: egocentric 256x256 RGB, relative position/odometry, previous action, goal category
setting.action_space: discrete: Forward 0.25 m, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (HSSD scenes, YCB objects); also a 2D gridworld, Memory Maze and T-Maze
setting.privileged: none at test time (geodesic distance is used only for the training reward and SPL computation)

numbers_note: Results are given only as curves in figures (ExtObjNav SR/SPL over 32k steps). The text gives only relative figures (Memo about +7.5% SR and +2.5% SPL over FCT on average, ~60% SR saturation) and a compute table (Memo 51.8 MB / 17.61 MFLOPs / 5.3 ms vs FCT 546.5 MB / 74.49 MFLOPs / 10.1 ms), so no per-benchmark metric tables are extractable.
results: On ExtObjNav (HSSD, 12 val scenes, 32k in-context steps), Memo beats the full-context transformer by 7.5% SR and 2.5% SPL on average while using 8x fewer context tokens, 10x less KV memory, 4.2x fewer FLOPs and 2x lower latency. It outperforms RMT by about 5% SR and AC with truncated backprop. In streaming evaluation Memo holds its performance while the transformer drops sharply. On Dark-Key-To-Door Memo matches FCT with more stable training.
limitations: Only evaluated on fixed-category object navigation in simulation; no semantic generalization to new categories, no real robot
Context-length extrapolation is still limited: Memo (16k) degrades after about 1.5x its training length, and performance saturates at about 60% SR
Sensitive to the summary length choice; no memory consolidation, and training is end-to-end from RL only without self-supervised objectives
